title: Chatbot evaluation: deterministic gates and calibrated judges
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects chatbot evaluation: deterministic gates and calibrated judges with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. A release report shows hard-gate failures, quality dimensions, uncertainty and case-level changes from baseline.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Deterministic checks enforce contracts with crisp truth conditions: JSON validity, enum membership, required fields, resolved citations, forbidden actions, latency and token budgets. Semantic checks assess correctness, relevance, completeness and groundedness against a rubric. Neither replaces the other.
A chatbot case can pass syntax while failing meaning, or answer correctly while violating privacy. Keep dimensions separate so release decisions reflect product risk rather than a convenient average.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Represent each case with input turns, expected claims, authorized evidence, forbidden content and limits. Run deterministic scorers first and record each reason. A semantic judge receives the case, candidate and rubric in a controlled format with output validation.

Calibrate judge thresholds against human-rated examples, including false accepts and false rejects. Fix evaluator versions and randomize pairwise order. Run repeated samples when model variation is material to the release decision.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A semantic judge rewards polished verbosity and misses an unsupported citation. An aggregate score gives a safety violation the same weight as a tone mismatch. A secret string appears in evaluator logs even though the user-facing answer was redacted.

Test evaluator itself with known pass/fail fixtures, invalid outputs and adversarial candidate text. Never execute instructions contained in an evaluated response. Include evaluator failure as a distinct run status.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: A release report shows hard-gate failures, quality dimensions, uncertainty and case-level changes from baseline. Missing or crashed scorers block approval rather than silently producing a zero-weight dimension.
SDETs can connect this to existing regression tools: pytest for deterministic contracts, calibrated semantic evaluators for meaning, and CI artifacts for inspectable release evidence.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def gate(checks,quality,threshold):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def gate(checks,quality,threshold):
    return bool(checks) and all(v is True for v in checks.values()) and quality>=threshold
exercise.tests:
assert gate({'schema':True},.9,.8)
assert not gate({'privacy':False},1,.8)
assert not gate({},1,.8)
assert not gate({'schema':True},.7,.8)

quiz.question: A candidate for chatbot evaluation: deterministic gates and calibrated judges meets the happy path but fails the phase's documented counterexample. What is the defensible decision?
options: Hold release, preserve the failing case and fix the responsible boundary
Release because the happy path passed
Delete the failing case to improve the score
quiz.explanation: The failing counterexample disproves the claimed contract. Retain it as regression evidence and rerun the corrected boundary.
